text: Among the faces, Brown recognized the most respected people of the village mingling freely with people of evil fame, but he saw no sign of Faith. <break time="0.8s" /> Bring forth the converts, cried a dark figure from the rock, and Brown was led forward by the minister and Deacon Gookin, while a veiled young woman was brought by Goody Cloyse. <break time="0.8s" /> Welcome, my children, to the communion of your race, said the dark figure, for now you shall know that those whom you have honored are as sinful as yourselves. <break time="0.8s" /> Evil is the nature of mankind, and evil must be your only happiness, he went on, as he prepared to mark their foreheads with a liquid from a hollow in the rock. <break time="0.8s" /> At that moment Brown cried out to his wife to look up to heaven and resist the wicked one, but whether Faith obeyed, he never knew. <break time="0.8s" /> Hardly had he spoken when he found himself alone amid calm night and solitude, and a hanging twig, which had been all on fire, sprinkled his cheek with the coldest dew. <break time="0.8s" /> The next morning, Brown came back into Salem village, and when Faith, with her pink ribbons, ran joyfully to meet him, he looked sternly at her and passed on without a greeting. <break time="0.8s" /> Perhaps Goodman Brown had only fallen asleep in the forest and dreamed a wild dream, but, alas, it was a dream of evil omen for young Goodman Brown. <break time="0.8s" /> A stern, sad, distrustful man he became from that night, and when he died after a long life, they carved no hopeful verse upon his tombstone, for his dying hour was gloom.
